title: A Garden for the Crown
premise: Silas Ravensworth carves bone charms that whisper with the voices of the dead, hiding her gift in a city where magic is punishable by unmaking. When a royal decree orders every gifted person hunted, Silas is dragged before the court—only to discover the king is already dead, his body puppeted by a crown-bound spirit that feeds on loyalty and lies. To free the realm, she must trace the crown's binding to its origin, ally with the very hunters sent to kill her, and choose between exposing a truth that will shatter the kingdom or preserving the lie that keeps it standing. In the end, Silas unbinds the crown at the cost of her own hearing—the dead fall silent to her forever—and she plants a garden over the old king's grave, finally belonging somewhere she chose herself.
about_author: Theo Voss is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing funeral customs across three continents before turning to fiction. They write about grief, inheritance, and the small magics people perform to survive being remembered.

chapters.title: The Quiet Trade
chapters.summary: Silas Ravensworth sells a mourning charm to a widow, letting the dead woman's husband speak one last time through carved bone. Her POV establishes her careful invisibility: no name spoken twice, no charm too powerful. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as safety. The chapter ends when a royal crier nails the Proclamation of Unmaking to her door.

chapters.title: Proclamation
chapters.summary: Silas burns her stock and plans to flee as hunters sweep the city. Through a dying neighbor's bones she learns the decree was issued in the king's voice—but the words carry no living breath. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into suspicion. She realizes the king may not be alive, and curiosity outweighs survival for the first time in five years.

chapters.title: What the Bones Remember
chapters.summary: Silas interrogates a grave-robber's stolen femur and hears fragments of a court physician's confession: something was bound into the crown decades ago. POV shifts briefly to Wren Calloway, a hunter who lets a gifted child escape and begins doubting his orders. Emotional beat: two searches converging on the same terrible question.

chapters.title: The Hunter's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Wren tracks Silas to her workshop but finds her mid-listening, weeping over a stranger's last words. Unable to arrest someone so human, he proposes an uneasy bargain: her knowledge of the dead for his protection from the hunt. Emotional beat: reluctant trust between natural enemies. Silas accepts because alone, she cannot reach the palace.

chapters.title: Ashes in the Ledger
chapters.summary: Traveling toward the capital, they stop in Silas's home village and find it razed—recorded in a hunter's ledger as 'cleansed.' Silas confronts the graves of family she abandoned to hide. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into resolve. She vows to unbind whatever wears the crown, even if it unmakes her.

chapters.title: The Gilded Court
chapters.summary: Disguised as a charm-smith summoned to court, Silas enters the palace and stands before King Aldric—whose body moves beautifully but whose bones are silent as river stones. She feels the crown listening back. Emotional beat: dread laced with awe. A courtier, Lady Maren, quietly slips her a warning note: 'It knows you came.'

chapters.title: Lady Maren's Bargain
chapters.summary: Maren reveals she serves a faction of nobles who suspect the truth and want the king freed—or replaced. She offers archives access in exchange for Silas carving a listening charm for their meetings. Emotional beat: the seduction and danger of allies with agendas. Silas agrees but hides the charm's true depth of hearing.

chapters.title: The Binding Rite
chapters.summary: In the sealed archive, Silas finds the original rite: the old queen bound her dying husband's spirit into the crown to preserve the succession—and the thing inside has since devoured three kings' souls. Emotional beat: horror at inheritance as a cage. The rite requires a willing vessel to undo it, and Silas understands why no one has tried.

chapters.title: Wren's Oath
chapters.summary: Wren is ordered to execute a captured gifted healer and refuses publicly, becoming hunted himself. He finds Silas bleeding from a hunter's blade and carries her through the sewers. Emotional beat: loyalty rewritten—he now serves the truth, not the crown. Their partnership hardens into something neither will name.

chapters.title: Voices in the Walls
chapters.summary: Recovering in Maren's wing, Silas listens to the palace itself through its foundation bones and hears generations of servants who died unseen. Among them, the first king's fragmentary ghost begs her to end it. Emotional beat: the weight of being the only one who can hear. She learns the crown must be removed while the vessel still lives.

chapters.title: The Feast of Loyalty
chapters.summary: At a state feast, the crown-thing senses Silas's gift and publicly commands her to carve a charm for the queen dowager—a trap. Under every noble's gaze, she carves a harmless trinket while secretly reading the room's dead. Emotional beat: performance under mortal threat. Maren covers for her, but the entity now hunts Silas specifically.

chapters.title: Betrayal in Bone
chapters.summary: One of Maren's faction sells them out; hunters raid the wing. Wren holds the corridor while Silas escapes through the servant bones' hidden passages, guided by the palace dead. Emotional beat: sacrifice and guilt—she survives because others bleed. Maren is taken, and Silas hears her screams through the walls all night.

chapters.title: The Dowager's Garden
chapters.summary: Silas seeks the queen dowager, rite's original author, now a recluse tending a walled garden. The old woman confesses everything: her husband begged to stay, and she could not let him go. Emotional beat: compassion for the original sin. She gives Silas the counter-rite and warns that the vessel must choose freely—no binding can be forced undone.

chapters.title: A King Who Cannot Die
chapters.summary: Silas reaches the current king's mind through a sliver of his own baby tooth, carved long ago. Inside, she finds Prince Aldric alive beneath decades of possession, barely himself. Emotional beat: fragile hope. He cannot simply say yes to freedom—the crown punishes dissent with agony—and Silas must find another way to give him choice.

chapters.title: The Hunt Closes
chapters.summary: With Maren imprisoned and Wren branded traitor, the pair hide in the bone-carvers' underground—a network of gifted folk Silas never knew existed. Emotional beat: belonging found too late, among people like her. They plan a coronation-anniversary ceremony where the king will be publicly crowned again, giving Silas one moment of proximity.

chapters.title: The Price of Hearing
chapters.summary: The counter-rite demands payment: the unbind er loses the gift entirely. Silas spends a night saying goodbye to the voices—the widow's husband, the palace dead, her mother's hum. Emotional beat: mourning a part of oneself while still alive. She chooses silence and a self-made life over a borrowed power.

chapters.title: Ceremony of Chains
chapters.summary: The anniversary ceremony begins; the crown-thing, suspicious, doubles the guard and searches faces. Wren creates a diversion by surrendering loudly, naming the true enemy before the assembled court. Emotional beat: courage as spectacle. Chaos erupts as half the court realizes the hunters have been hunting the wrong monsters.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Amid the riot, Silas reaches the throne and begins the counter-rite as the crown-thing pours its fury through the king's body. Aldric, feeling her carve the final line into a charm pressed to his brow, finds one free breath—and chooses. Emotional beat: climax of will against will. The crown cracks; the entity shrieks out of the world.

chapters.title: The Silence After
chapters.summary: The king collapses alive but hollow; the dead are gone from Silas's ears forever. She wakes in a cell awaiting judgment as the court decides what truth to tell. Emotional beat: exhaustion and strange peace. Wren testifies; Maren, freed, forces the council to hear the whole history rather than bury it.

chapters.title: Truth Before the Throne
chapters.summary: Aldric, recovering, addresses the kingdom: he confesses the possession, ends the hunt, and pardons the gifted. Some nobles resist; the garden network of carvers steps into daylight for the first time. Emotional beat: a nation choosing uncomfortable truth over comfortable lie. Silas watches, deaf to the dead but hearing the living clearly for once.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Aldric offers Silas a title and a place at court; she declines both, asking instead for the dowager's walled garden and a plot of land. Wren, discharged, asks what she'll do with quiet. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not granted. She begins turning the garden's soil where the old king will finally be buried.

chapters.title: A Garden for the Crown
chapters.summary: Spring. Silas plants the garden over the first king's grave, the cracked crown melted into a bell that rings only in wind. Wren visits with bread and no agenda; the carving community thrives openly in the city below. Emotional beat: resolution—grief composted into growth. In the silence where voices used to be, Silas finally hears herself.
